correctness.rationale: Every palindrome has an odd run count. A subsequence using all \(2k+1\) source runs corresponds bijectively to choices of matching paired exponents, giving \(a_{k+1}\prod_{i=1}^{k}\min(a_i,a_{2k+2-i})\). The AM–GM bound is sharp at leading order, while all shorter-run palindromes number at most \(2\sum_{j=0}^{k-1} n^{j+1}\). Exact one-/three-run counts, a complete four-case inequality, and witnesses establish \(n+\lfloor n^2/8\rfloor\) for three and four host runs. The script checked 1,365 run compositions, 3,807 direct-vs-dynamic-programming word instances, and 32 constructions. Infinite correctness rests on the written proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The general Fibonacci upper bound is too coarse to force an exact polynomial leading coefficient for fixed binary run count. The large-alphabet regime \(q\ge n/2\) excludes growing \(n\) on a fixed binary alphabet except for small lengths. Longest-subsequence results concern a different invariant.

evidence: The 2021 theorem upper-bounds all binary words exponentially in length, and its fixed-q result applies when q is at least half the length.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: An exponential envelope does not imply an exact leading coefficient in the polynomially growing fixed-run subclass; an existence theorem for a long subsequence cannot determine the number of distinct palindromic subsequences. The new full-run product and low-run equality are neither direct corollaries nor reparameterizations of the inspected primary statements.

originality.rationale: Three highly relevant full-text papers were inspected; the 2021 count bounds are indexed by length/alphabet, the 2009 structural paper studies the palindrome set and longest-word/extension invariants, and the 2019 paper studies longest subsequences. Run-constrained sharp cardinality extrema and their polynomial leading coefficients were not identified. Literature-screen incompleteness is acknowledged.

value.rationale: Run count is a canonical structural parameter of finite binary words; imposing it reveals exact polynomial growth with optimal exponent and leading coefficient for every fixed odd run count, unlike the general exponential upper envelope. The sharp all-length equality of the three- and four-run maxima supplies an additional nonobvious structural boundary. The objects and invariants precede the computation, and the theorem gives a complete asymptotic family rather than an isolated slice.
